# ExamGuard AI Remote Proctoring System Specification

## Intended Use and Context
ExamGuard analyzes real-time webcam feeds, audio streams, and desktop activity during high-stakes university exams, automatically flagging cheating behaviors.

## Risk Management (Article 9)
A preliminary risk management log was drafted during initial deployment. Periodic reviews occur after examination seasons.

## Data Governance (Article 10)
Training datasets consist of 10,000 hours of volunteer exam video recordings scraped from laboratory pilot studies.

## Bias Examination & Mitigation (Article 10(2)(f))
Bias examination across varied skin tones, lighting conditions, and facial neurodivergence is untested. False positive cheating alerts are unmitigated across underrepresented student demographics.

## Technical Documentation (Article 11)
Internal user manuals and API documentation exist on company Confluence wikis.

## Automated Logging (Article 12)
Server access logs capture student login sessions and flag events.

## Transparency (Article 13)
Students receive a brief terms of service disclaimer prior to launching the exam browser extension.

## Human Oversight (Article 14)
The system automatically revokes student test access upon detecting three suspicious gaze anomalies. No human proctor confirmation is required before exam disqualification, and an emergency stop kill switch is absent.

## Robustness and Cybersecurity (Article 15)
The system utilizes standard HTTPS encryption for video streaming. Adversarial evasion attacks such as virtual camera spoofing remain unaddressed.
